geo.label: tariff shock / growth scare
parts: Macro Stance

US equities have slipped into correction, and the trigger is tariff policy more than the data. The S&P 500 closed at 5,521.52 index points, down 8.76% over 20 sessions and 3.78% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). CNN framed the day as the Dow sliding and the S&P 500 closing in correction as the trade war escalated [[n11858]]. Goldman Sachs cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 6,200 on weaker profit forecasts [[n3031]], while Citi kept 6,500 as its base case [[n11685]], so the sell-side split is about how much earnings damage tariffs will do, not about the direction of the tape. The growth data are softer than the prices. February CPI came in at 2.8%, under consensus [[n11278]], and payrolls rose 151,000, below expectations [[n10960]]. Powell said the Fed is in no hurry to adjust rates while policy uncertainty runs high [[n11433]]. The VIX closed at 24.66, up 55.19% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and a J.P. Morgan economist puts the US recession odds at 40% [[n0529]].
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.94% and the 10Y at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13), leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +33 bps. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 42 bps and the 10Y fell 35 bps, so the spread widened 7 bps. The curve is positively sloped, and the 20-observation move is bull steepening, with the front end rallying harder than the long end (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13). The 30Y sits at 4.59%, 24 bps lower over 20 observations, which is a rally led by the policy path rather than a term-premium shock. TLT is up 3.92% over 20 sessions while HYG is down 1.00%, so the bid is in duration rather than credit (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The dollar index stands at 103.83 index points, down 3.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the recent dollar decline a natural ‘adjustment’ [[n4051]].
New / Most Important

The most important near-term item is the funding deadline. The New York Times reports that Schumer will clear the way for the Republican spending bill, breaking with his party [[n11891]], and Senate Democrats signalled they will advance the bill to avoid a shutdown [[n11899]]. CNN put the stakes as what is at risk if Congress does not fund the government by Friday [[n11929]]. A shutdown would arrive in the same week the tariff escalation has already pushed the index into correction. CNBC’s argument that markets have learned to ignore shutdowns [[n11876]] is the bull case, but it carries less weight when tariffs are already compressing earnings expectations.
Playbook ✓

Keep duration as the hedge and do not add cyclical equity until the funding vote and the tariff talks clear. Own the long end only while the curve keeps bull steepening, and trim high-beta Nasdaq exposure until the Nasdaq 100 recovers its 20-session reference of 21,719.26 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The call changes if the VIX returns toward its level of 15.89 from 20 sessions earlier and the stopgap clears without a tariff escalation (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

geo.label: fiscal pivot / easing bias
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is easing into a tariff shock with its policy rate already falling. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% in early March [[n3354]] and described policy as ‘meaningfully less restrictive’ [[n3356]]. The first risk is that the trade shock hits Germany: the Bundesbank chief said US tariffs could extend Germany’s recession [[n3602]]. The fiscal turn is the offset. Markets rallied when Berlin moved to lift the debt brake for defence and infrastructure [[n3341]], and the shift has been called Germany’s ‘whatever it takes’ moment [[n3387]]. JPMorgan raised its euro-area 2025 growth forecast, joining Goldman [[n3467]]. The DAX is down 0.20% over 20 sessions against 3.13% for the Euro Stoxx 50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the German core is holding up better than the bloc.
Credit & Inflation

Inflation is cooling. Euro-area inflation dipped to 2.4% in February, and the ECB bets point to a sixth rate cut [[n3317]]. Lagarde warned that trade and defence shocks risk amplifying inflation [[n3566]], and that higher defence spending could push it up [[n3559]]. France is the credit pressure point, with borrowing costs near a 14-year high before a Fitch review [[n3584]]. Bund safe-haven status is holding in swaps even as German spending worries mount [[n3503]].
New / Most Important

Trade retaliation has moved from threat to action. The EU will impose counter-tariffs on $28 billion of US goods [[n11761]], and Trump answered with a threatened 200% tariff on European wine after the EU proposed a whiskey tax [[n11914]]. The US trade representative issued a statement on the EU’s retaliatory tariffs [[n11745]]. US importers of EU wine are already warning of closures and layoffs [[n9753]].
Playbook ✓

Own German fiscal beneficiaries on dips, the infrastructure and industrial suppliers that gain from the spending plan, and keep the defence leaders as the cash-flow anchor. Avoid European autos until the tariff path is settled. The call changes if the counter-tariffs are shelved, which would lift autos, or if the Bundesbank’s warning turns into an orders downgrade, which would turn the German overweight into a trim.

geo.label: stimulus vs deflation
parts: Macro Stance

China is trying to hold growth near its target while deflation keeps deepening. The 5% growth goal sets the frame, and South China Morning Post opinion asks where that growth will come from [[n1382]]. The annual Congress closed with questions still open about how to revive a slowing economy [[n1345]]. The stimulus on the table is a $41 billion consumption plan, which CNBC calls just a start as deflationary pressures deepen [[n1196]]. CNN says deflation problems are getting worse [[n1207]], and Bloomberg asks why China cannot escape the cycle [[n1497]]. Policy direction is supportive, but the price data are not confirming it, so the stance is Mixed.
PMIs & Activity

The most recent activity print is February’s non-manufacturing PMI at 50.4, a reading just above the expansion line for services and construction [[n0845]]. That is a positive but thin signal, and it sits against the deflation reading. The view is confirmed if the next non-manufacturing PMI holds above 50 while consumer prices stay in deflation. A drop back below 50 would confirm the bear case that the consumption plan is too small for the demand gap. The index level, not the trend, is the signal today.
Credit Impulse

Credit is the weakest part of the picture, and the evidence is about stress rather than volume. China’s bond yields jumped to three-month highs as investors pared rate-cut expectations [[n1188]]. Evergrande and other units were ordered to repay $1.8 billion of deposit pledges [[n1337]], and some Hong Kong banks are refusing home loans for Vanke’s Le Mont project in Tai Po [[n1394]]. Higher yields with cuts priced out are the opposite of a credit impulse. The read rests on the yield move and the lender retreat, which is enough to keep the credit call negative.
Property

Property is still in adjustment, and policy is steering toward quality over volume. A State Council piece frames the new vision as quality homes amid market adjustment [[n1558]], and analysts warn that the push for better homes adds stress for developers [[n1446]]. A minister says the sector is showing positive changes [[n1155]], which is the official line. Hong Kong’s property slump is pushing hotels toward student housing [[n5387]], a sign of how long the pressure lasts. Turnover is the constraint on any rebound, and the policy direction does not change that in the near term.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy is leaning on trade management rather than domestic demand. China’s tariffs on US farm products took effect [[n1442]], and Beijing took issue with the US linking tariffs to fentanyl [[n1515]]. The commerce ministry met Walmart over supplier pricing [[n9436]], a domestic pricing step that shows the government is watching retailers’ costs. A summit between Trump and Xi is being discussed for June [[n1359]], which keeps a negotiation channel open. The fiscal anchor is the 5% growth goal, so the next signal is whether Beijing sizes support above the $41 billion consumption plan [[n1196]].
Markets & Flows

Equities are the bright spot. The Hang Seng closed at 23,462.65 index points, up 7.56% over 20 sessions though down 0.58% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The Shanghai Composite is at 3,358.73 index points, up 0.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Hong Kong’s market has been booming while Wall Street is in turmoil [[n11869]], and ADR premiums for Chinese names are widening as the stock rerating continues [[n1526]]. The China large-cap ETF (FXI) is up 7.08% over 20 sessions and the internet ETF (KWEB) is up 5.87% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Chinese stocks and emerging-market debt drew large inflows in February [[n1528]], and mainland investors bought a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1243]]. The currency is firmer: USD/CNY closed at 7.2371, down 0.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the offshore yuan climbed to a four-month high [[n1477]].
New / Most Important

The new signal is the gap between the stimulus size and the deflation problem. The $41 billion consumption plan [[n1196]] sits beside a 5% growth goal, and the market is reading it as a start rather than a fix. The equity leg is being carried by AI. Alibaba released an AI model that reads emotions to take on OpenAI [[n1421]], and its chairman Joe Tsai argues that consumers’ $20 trillion of savings is the growth lever China needs [[n1447]]. The next change to the view comes from policy. If Beijing extends consumption support beyond this plan, the deflation read improves; if it does not, the equity rally runs ahead of the economy.
Playbook ✓

Own the equity beta in Hong Kong internet and AI names on dips, keep duration neutral, and avoid property developers until the credit data confirm a turn. Keep yuan exposure small above the four-month high. The call changes if the consumption plan is extended and the PMI holds above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng is up 7.56% over 20 sessions while the credit and property reads are still negative (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).

geo.label: BOJ hike bias / tariff drag
parts: Macro Stance

Japan’s rate path is tightening into a weak growth patch. The 10-year yield reached its highest level since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5305]], and Reuters reports that a rate-hike discussion could come in May if inflation risks persist [[n5238]]. Growth is softer: the economy downgraded its fourth-quarter GDP [[n5308]], and services sentiment soured on the cost of living [[n5310]]. Wages are the reason the BOJ leans hawkish. Major firms agreed large pay increases [[n5398]], and the largest union group sought its biggest wage increase in over 30 years [[n5240]]. The Nikkei 225 sits at 36,790.03 index points, down 5.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 148.2790, down 3.87% over 20 sessions, which means the yen has strengthened against the dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The yen is also being bid as a haven: one strategist calls it the new safe-haven currency [[n5272]], while Kuroda warned that Japan must fix the impression that it manipulates the yen [[n5254]]. The tariff track is unhelpful. Japan’s trade minister did not win a tariff exemption assurance [[n5311]], and the prime minister’s gifts apology clouded the budget outlook [[n5421]]. Toyota is down 2.89% over 20 sessions and Sony is up 3.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so exporter shares are not moving as one.
Playbook ✓

Favour banks and domestic wage beneficiaries over exporters while the BOJ path is live, and use yen longs as the hedge for exporter exposure. Avoid adding long-duration JGBs at 2008-high yields until the May discussion is clearer. The call changes if the tariff talks produce a concrete exemption or if the yen reverses above its 20-session reference of 154.2550 (2025-02-13).

geo.label: cuts done / iron ore drag
parts: Macro Stance

Australia’s growth is turning up from a low base. The economy exited a 21-month per capita recession [[n0157]], and Bloomberg reports that growth accelerated, which backs the RBA’s hawkish tone [[n0159]]. The RBA cut in February [[n0075]], and the governor has played down the chance of more cuts [[n0073]]. Tariffs are the drag. Albanese called US tariffs ‘not a friendly act’ [[n0333]], and Trump has said Australia’s hope of an exemption is fading [[n1289]]. Canberra says it will not retaliate [[n11747]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.6328, up 0.71% over 20 sessions, so the currency is holding up despite the tariff noise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The ASX 200 is at 7,749.10 index points, down 9.26% over 20 sessions and 4.27% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). BlackRock cut its exposure to Australian shares on value grounds [[n0260]], and the iron ore chain is under pressure from China’s steel cuts [[n0251]]. BHP is down 6.71% over 20 sessions and Fortescue 19.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The central bank has also raised concern about banks’ plan to shut a key payments system [[n0428]].
Playbook ✓

Hold the miners on pullbacks only while iron ore holds, underweight the banks against the ASX 200’s drawdown, and keep the AUD long as the tariff hedge. The call flips if China’s steel cuts reverse and the miners lead the index back up. A break in the Australian dollar’s own trend would change the currency view, not the equity one.

geo.label: hold / strong zloty
parts: Macro Stance

The Polish economy is turning up. The manufacturing PMI signalled a recovery in industry and an end to a nearly three-year recession [[n5785]]. The central bank governor, Glapiński, said there are no reasons to cut rates now [[n5581]], and said the fall in inflation is still a ‘dość odległy horyzont’, a distant horizon [[n6126]]. The rate path is therefore a hold. Parkiet argues it is not the time for emotion around the monetary council, the RPP [[n6076]], while Business Insider Polska frames the next decision as relief for borrowers arriving [[n6055]]. The labour data conflict. Eurostat put Poland at a record-low unemployment rate, joint-lowest in the EU [[n10792]], while the labour ministry explains a rise in unemployment [[n5975]], so the labour market gets no directional call. Official wage data are positive, with GUS reporting 2024 pay figures that show higher earnings [[n5786]].
Markets

The zloty is the strongest asset in the block. USD/PLN closed at 3.8452, down 3.93% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.1838 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The euro was at its cheapest against the zloty since 2018 [[n5777]], and Bloomberg reported that the zloty surged to a 10-year high on a hawkish central bank [[n5467]]. The governor also made an unambiguous statement on whether the central bank would intervene in the currency [[n6120]]. Equities are following. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 50.96 PLN, up 3.44% over 20 sessions, and the iShares MSCI Poland ETF at 27.58 USD, up 7.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions and PKO 3.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is leaning toward defence. EU ministers backed a temporary exemption for defence spending from the EU’s budget rules [[n5531]], and a Credit Agricole economist says the Union is moving toward looser fiscal rules [[n6010]]. The VAT gap fell unexpectedly last year, which helps the budget arithmetic [[n6074]]. Politically, the far-right candidate has moved into second place in the presidential race [[n5515]], and Biejat, who says she would tidy up the mortgage market as president, is pitching on housing [[n5905]]. The US has said it will retaliate if Poland introduces a tax on big tech [[n5527]].
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news is strong, and buybacks are the common thread. Allegro expects 2025 earnings growth and proposed a $364 million buyback [[n5576]], and the Polish press reports double-digit profit growth, with the company saying it has proved it can deliver [[n6115]]. Allegro closed at 32.38 PLN, up 13.61% in the prior session and 11.02% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). PKO BP’s results show Poland’s largest bank boasting a profit jump of almost 4 billion zloty [[n6136]], and a record dividend is being discussed [[n6145]]; the shares closed at 74.02 PLN, up 3.32% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Orlen still lacks a final agreement with Sołowow on the small-nuclear project [[n6140]], yet Orlen is up 16.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Dino Polska is hiring 1,300 people [[n6122]] and its shares are at a record high [[n5823]]. KGHM’s chief executive says years of neglect and no investment are the problem [[n5868]], and the stock is down 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Geopolitics & Security

Security is the louder narrative. Polish President Duda urged the US to move nuclear warheads onto Polish territory, the FT reported [[n5584]], and told the BBC that US nuclear weapons in Poland would be a deterrent for Russia [[n5572]]. Warsaw wants 100,000 volunteers for military training in 2027 [[n5546]] and has asked NATO to raise the minimum defence spending to 3% of GDP [[n5485]]. Prosecutors say Russia used a spy posing as a Belarusian refugee to set a Warsaw mall on fire [[n5565]]. Washington’s line is blunter: Rubio told Poland to ‘say thank you’ amid the Starlink spat over Ukraine [[n5504]].
New / Most Important

The one signal that matters is that defence is now both a budget and a currency story. The EU’s temporary carve-out [[n5531]] and the 3% NATO request [[n5485]] turn defence into a multi-year fiscal commitment. Speculative equity money is following: Bankier reports that steel and armaments names have taken over speculative attention on the Warsaw exchange [[n5977]], and a separate Bankier piece says the defence sector is trading on the military rally [[n5840]]. For investors the meaning is that the Polish equity move increasingly depends on military budgets rather than on the consumer.
Playbook ✓

Own the zloty winners with dividend and buyback support, PKO and Allegro, and keep the defence names as a tactical trade rather than a core holding. Hedge a zloty long against a surprise shift in the central bank’s tone, even though the governor has ruled out reasons to cut for now. The call changes if USD/PLN climbs back above its reference of 4.0026 from 13 February (Yahoo Finance). ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 tracker is up 3.44% over 20 sessions while KGHM is down 2.75% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Narrative

The consensus says AI demand keeps technology earnings compounding, while the 20-session tape says the market is repricing monetisation. The Technology Select Sector SPDR is at 207.66 USD, down 11.94% over 20 sessions and 1.90% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver that matters now is whether software and AI spending can show revenue, not just usage, and Reuters reports that Adobe’s dull forecast raised AI monetisation doubts [[n3006]].
Reported

Adobe beat on its first quarter, but its revenue outlook disappointed and the stock fell [[n3106]]. CNBC put the drop at 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed the beat [[n3109]], and Adobe is down 13.85% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Oracle’s sales missed estimates even as its chief executive pointed to AI-driven growth [[n0492]]. Workday’s full-year EPS missed expectations [[n3183]].
EPS Upside Watch

The set-up for a surprise is in AI infrastructure rather than application software. ServiceNow agreed a record $2.9 billion deal for Moveworks [[n6339]], and Broadcom’s call highlighted record revenue and AI growth [[n2684]]. Suppliers are lining up announcements for the 2025 Nvidia GTC conference [[n9560]], which gives the chain a pending showcase.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Nvidia held up better than its Magnificent Seven peers during Thursday’s rout [[n6603]], which cuts against the idea that AI leaders are de-rating in lockstep. Nvidia closed at 115.58 USD, down 11.87% over 20 sessions but up 4.53% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Narrative

The consensus is that ad-supported platforms and streaming keep growing. The Communication Services SPDR is at 94.84 USD, down 8.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is the swing name, down 18.58% over 20 sessions and 4.67% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Ad budgets are under pressure too: Sirius XM fell 8.6% as its ad sales collapsed [[n11174]].
Reported

Telecoms flagged softness, and Verizon and AT&T shares slid after both signalled near-term weakness [[n6471]]. Netflix is down 13.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Meta is launching Community Notes in the US [[n9584]], a product step rather than a reported result.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside lever is creator monetisation. Facebook now lets creators get paid for views on stories [[n3138]], which adds revenue at the margin, though it is small against the ad-budget squeeze. Spotify’s $10 billion payment to the music industry shows the royalty cost base is rising [[n3070]], which limits the streaming upside.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Telecom is the exception to the sector’s weakness. Verizon is up 7.85% and AT&T 2.88% over 20 sessions while the sector ETF is down 8.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the defensive bid is working inside a sector that is supposed to be growth.
Narrative

The consensus is that banks are cheap on capital return. The Financial Select SPDR is at 47.42 USD, down 7.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The driver is recession pricing and credit: US corporate bond spreads hit their widest in about six months on recession fears [[n3950]], and Goldman Sachs says spreads will get a lot wider amid tariffs [[n3916]]. JPMorgan is down 18.25% over 20 sessions and Goldman Sachs 19.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Reported

Bank stocks tumbled as recession fears rose [[n0508]], and Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and SoFi were hit hardest in the Monday sell-off [[n6272]]. Bank of America cut 150 junior investment-banking jobs [[n11210]], a cost signal rather than a loss signal. Goldman’s 2024 results beat expectations [[n2213]], an older print that still anchors the group’s earnings base.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside case rests on cost discipline and trading. Bank of America’s cuts [[n11210]] and the Stifel regulatory fine [[n9711]] show the group trimming costs, and the volatility of the tariff tape is the usual driver of trading desks’ revenue, so a surprise would come from trading activity.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Berkshire Hathaway is up 6.89% over 20 sessions while the sector falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Warren Buffett’s ‘keep your head’ advice in a falling market reached a wide audience [[n11599]]. Berkshire is acting as the shelter in this tape.
Narrative

The consensus is that OPEC+ supply and softer demand keep crude range-bound. WTI closed at 66.55 USD, down 6.75% over 20 sessions, while the energy ETF is up 1.42% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The IEA’s March oil market report is the demand reference [[n9634]], and oil settled lower on tariff worry and supply-demand expectations [[n9638]].
Reported

The sector’s corporate news is about structure rather than results. Whitecap and Veren merged, reshaping the Canadian energy landscape [[n9784]], and Shell rose while the market fell [[n3163]]. The reported move is in the share reaction, not the commodity.
EPS Upside Watch

Record OPEC+ fuel exports blunt the group’s crude supply cut [[n9676]], which caps the price upside. The upside case is in gas: Henry Hub closed at 4.11 USD, up 15.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and AI and LNG demand are expected to keep US gas use at record highs [[n9357]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Russia’s high-flying gas exporter is crippled as Europe stays away [[n11885]], and the US has sanctioned Iran’s oil minister and the shadow fleet [[n4976]]. Those are supply-side tailwinds that crude is not showing, since WTI is down 6.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Narrative

The consensus is that industrials lose to tariffs but win on spending. The Industrial Select SPDR is at 128.78 USD, down 6.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The tariffs are landing: the steel and aluminium tariffs took effect and set off global retaliation [[n9748]], and US physical aluminium premiums hit a record [[n11916]].
Reported

Delta cut its profit forecast on macro uncertainty [[n2900]], and its shares fell after the outlook cut [[n2901]]. Rheinmetall rose 7% on its results and the European defence boost [[n3062]], and its full-year call highlighted record growth [[n9680]].
EPS Upside Watch

Defence is the set-up. European money managers are starting to bring defence stocks in from the cold [[n3580]], and that flow supports the sector’s valuation. In the US, Lockheed Martin is up 5.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a relative bright spot for the sector.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Boeing’s supply problems are sharper than the tariff story. Faulty parts on 787 jets flew below the radar in Italy [[n9532]], and AerCap’s chief executive said a 787 could rise $40 million in cost in the worst case [[n8668]]. Boeing is down 14.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), while the aerospace and defence ETF is down 4.78% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Narrative

The consensus is that the US consumer is resilient. The Consumer Discretionary SPDR is at 192.60 USD, down 13.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The WSJ says consumer angst is striking all income levels [[n9448]], and Dollar General’s chief executive says shoppers only have enough money for basic essentials [[n3989]].
Reported

American Eagle said the consumer is slowing and issued weak guidance [[n3010]], and Ulta issued weak guidance, citing consumer uncertainty and its own missteps [[n3175]]. Dick’s Sporting Goods is the latest retailer to forecast a rocky 2025 [[n0502]]. Hugo Boss warned of lingering uncertainty amid weak consumer sentiment [[n11340]].
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in the names with a self-help story. Dick’s 2024 earnings per share rose 15% [[n2899]], and its Gamechanger app is adding $100 million of revenue as media ventures grow [[n3024]]. Those are the places a surprise can still come from in a sector where the guidance has been cut.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consumer weakness is being traded as a positive for discount names: Dollar General and Dollar Tree rose as penny-pinching consumers look for low-cost options [[n4002]]. Tesla, the most-discussed name in the retail debate, is down 28.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the trade-down is not lifting the discretionary leaders.
Narrative

The consensus is that staples are the defensive shelter. The Consumer Staples SPDR is at 79.33 USD, down 1.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the shelter has held better than the rest of the market. The driver is trade-down: Dollar General warned that American shoppers are struggling [[n3993]].
Reported

Dollar General’s sales guidance came in higher than estimates [[n3129]], while its store review and closures dented fourth-quarter earnings [[n3130]]. Costco stock suffered its biggest one-day drop in over three years [[n3022]], and the shares closed at 890.62 USD, down 16.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
EPS Upside Watch

The upside case is in discount and value formats, where trade-down spending moves volume [[n4002]]. Dollar General’s sales guidance above estimates [[n3129]] makes it the clearest upside watch in the group, although its store closures are a cost headwind.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Walmart is down 18.44% over 20 sessions even as trade-down should favour it, and China’s commerce ministry met Walmart over supplier pricing [[n9436]]. Walmart closed at 84.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the largest US retailer is being squeezed on costs and on pricing.
Narrative

The consensus is that healthcare is defensive growth with a pharma tariff overhang. The Health Care SPDR is at 143.83 USD, down 1.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a relative shelter. The main driver is obesity drugs: Eli Lilly is down 8.17% over 20 sessions while Merck is up 10.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the Eli Lilly chief executive’s pay reflects the obesity-drug franchise [[n2912]].
Reported

Mallinckrodt and Endo’s $6.7 billion merger is getting a bump from tariffs [[n4896]], and Ireland could lose its pharma tax advantage to the US after the president’s accusations [[n3143]]. Merck opened a billion-dollar US facility to make Gardasil [[n3807]], which is a reshoring move in the sector.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside sits with names whose tariff exposure is small and whose franchises are growing. Gilead is a hedge-fund favourite in the pharma group [[n9788]], and Vertex is up 10.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the defensive bid is working in the large caps.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Hims & Hers, Zealand and Roche fell as weight-loss stocks sold off [[n6585]], even as microdosing of weight-loss drugs goes viral and worries experts [[n9585]]. Novo Nordisk’s US listing is down 7.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the obesity theme is being sold through the names even as the trend draws attention.
Narrative

The consensus is that materials are a tariff-price story. The Materials SPDR is at 84.87 USD, down 4.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), but the metals are rising. Gold closed at 2,991.30 USD, up 2.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Reuters reports that gold scaled a record high and is sprinting toward $3,000 [[n9506]]. Copper is an asset here: Citigroup sees LME copper reaching $10,000 before tariffs bite [[n9446]], and copper closed at 4.90 USD a pound, up 4.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Reported

Anglo American began consultation to cut jobs as it overhauls its business [[n11305]]. Newmont rose 4.63% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a gold-equity move that tracks the metal’s record.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside set-up is in metals with price-setting power. US physical aluminium premiums reached a record as tariffs bite [[n11916]], which lifts margins for domestic producers. Freeport-McMoRan rose 2.18% in the prior session, and the copper miners ETF is up 1.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Iron ore is the counter-signal. China’s steel cuts are piling pressure on Australian iron ore [[n0251]], and Singapore iron ore rose on hopes of stronger Chinese demand [[n0378]]. The bullish tilt needs the metal to hold while the steel chain shrinks.
Narrative

The consensus is that real estate is a rates trade. The Real Estate SPDR is at 40.66 USD, down 2.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The 10Y is 35 bps lower over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13), and mortgage rates are at three-month lows [[n11358]]. Rocket’s deal for Redfin could make home buying more convenient, and more expensive [[n11370]].
Reported

Redfin’s shares spiked on the Rocket deal, which is valued at $1.75 billion [[n11070]], the sector’s main corporate event. Yahoo reports that mortgage rates are down 37 basis points this year [[n10996]].
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in rate-sensitive housing names if the 20-observation rally holds. Tariffs add as much as $10,000 to the cost of the average new home, a trade association says [[n1564]], which caps the volume recovery and keeps the upside to margin rather than volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Falling mortgage rates and rising build costs are pulling in opposite directions. The rate tailwind is real, while tariffs add to the cost of the product being financed [[n1564]], so the sector can rally on rates and still see housing volume stall.
Narrative

The consensus is that utilities are the AI power trade. The Utilities SPDR is at 77.36 USD, down 2.38% over 20 sessions but up 1.95% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Amazon, Google and Meta support tripling nuclear power by 2050 [[n6479]], which is the long-run demand case for the sector.
Reported

The data-centre build-out is stressing the grid. Reuters reports fears that the build-out could overburden the biggest US grid [[n9464]], and the PJM transmission outlook has been lifted by data-centre growth [[n11068]]. Dominion Energy’s data-centre catalysts make it a buy in one analyst view [[n2908]].
EPS Upside Watch

The regulated names are picking up the demand story without the merchant premium. Duke Energy is up 2.93% over five sessions and Southern Company 3.25% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The upside watch is regulated earnings growth from power-demand contracts.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The merchant names with the largest AI exposure are the ones being sold. Constellation Energy is down 33.12% over 20 sessions and Vistra 29.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), while the regulated names rise, so the sector’s AI premium is not evenly distributed.
Narrative

The consensus is that European carmakers are cheap on the assumption that tariffs are negotiable. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts ETF is at 51.51 EUR, down 6.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The tariffs are landing on the cost base: BMW will absorb tariff costs on some Mexican-built models [[n4712]], and S&P downgraded Stellantis on expected tariff headwinds [[n2639]].
Reported

Volkswagen plans to lay off 1,600 staff at its Cariad software unit [[n3879]], Porsche’s earnings per share were cut by a third in 2024 [[n3060]], and the list of automakers cutting jobs includes Porsche, GM and Ford [[n3172]]. European truck shares fell after the US reversed an electric-vehicle rule [[n3581]].
EPS Upside Watch

The upside set-up is in Volkswagen’s outlook rather than its print. Volkswagen Group reported solid full-year 2024 results with a robust outlook [[n0520]], and the preferred shares are up 7.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The surprise would be a tariff-cost guide that is better than feared.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Volkswagen’s US ADR is up 16.65% over 20 sessions even as the sector falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and Ford’s $4.8 billion German revamp is a bet on the European plant base [[n9491]]. The stock-level reversal is what the sector narrative misses.
Narrative

The consensus is that AI capex supports chips. The semiconductor ETF is at 195.10 USD, down 11.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the PHLX Semiconductor Index is down 12.52% over 20 sessions at 4,453.24 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). TSMC pitched an Intel foundry joint venture to Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom [[n8806]], and Taiwanese stocks suffered record foreign selling as TSMC was dumped [[n9157]].
Reported

Intel jumped nearly 15% on the appointment of its new chief executive [[n9539]], and the WSJ profiled the approach of ‘disrupt and leapfrog’ [[n9797]]. Micron has sampled 1γ DDR5 with reduced EUV use [[n8604]], a process step that matters for memory costs.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in memory and equipment. Micron’s memory cycle is described as prolonged [[n2942]], and ASML and imec are partnering on sub-2nm process tools [[n8661]]. Huawei’s Ascend 910C is being pitched against Nvidia in China [[n1581]], which is a competition risk to the upside.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Intel is up 14.60% in the prior session while the sector’s index fell 0.62% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a single-name turnaround the sector ETF does not share.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance decides the reaction, not the quarter
parts: Rewarded

Allegro’s 2025 earnings outlook and its $364 million buyback drew the buyers, and the shares are up 13.61% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13) [[n5576]]. Dollar General rose on sales guidance above estimates [[n3129]], and its shares and Dollar Tree’s rose as penny-pinching consumers looked for low-cost options [[n4002]]. Intel’s stock jumped on the leadership change [[n9542]], which the market treated as a turnaround signal rather than a reported result.
Punished

Adobe beat its first quarter, but its revenue outlook disappointed and the shares slid 13.85% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13) [[n3006]]. Costco had its biggest one-day drop in more than three years [[n3022]] and is down 16.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Marvell’s shares tumbled despite strong AI revenue growth [[n2941]], and the stock is down 34.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Oracle’s sales missed estimates [[n0492]], and its shares are down 14.26% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Pattern

Beats are not enough when the guidance is soft. Adobe, Oracle and Marvell all showed revenue or AI growth and were still sold, while the names raising outlooks, Allegro and Dollar General, were bought. The market pays for forward revenue visibility and punishes the guide, not the quarter. The consumer names were the clearest case: American Eagle issued weak guidance [[n3010]], and Ulta did the same [[n3175]], so the outlook cut is the event that matters.
Attention into EPS

Attention is on guidance language into the next prints. The Dollar General and Adobe reactions set the bar: investors reward a guide above consensus and punish a revenue outlook that frames AI as a cost. The next scheduled attention point in the AI chain is the Nvidia GTC showcase [[n9560]], and the memory-cycle debate is the second thread [[n2942]].
Playbook

Own the guidance raisers into the next print, Allegro and Dollar General, sell rallies in Adobe, where the outlook sets a bar the business may not clear, and hold off adding to Costco until wage costs are clearer. Avoid chasing the first-day bounce in a name with soft guidance. The pattern flips if an AI-software name raises revenue guidance above consensus, since the market has so far treated AI revenue as a cost line.

underowned.title: German infrastructure beyond defence
parts: Attention Gap

Attention is on German defence, but the spending plan is wider. Euronews argues that stocks will gain from Germany’s economic revolution beyond defence [[n3576]], and the fiscal boost has already sparked a market rally [[n3387]]. The defence trade gets the attention, while the infrastructure and industrial suppliers that build the spending get less of the crowd’s attention.
Exposure & Risk

The exposure is the broad European and German equity lines and the industrial suppliers. The Euro Stoxx 50 is down 3.13% over 20 sessions while the DAX is down 0.20% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the FTSE 100 is down 2.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The risk is that the spending plan gets delayed by the same tariff shock that the Bundesbank has warned could extend the recession [[n3602]].
Trigger to Watch

A German budget or procurement announcement that names infrastructure and industrial lines would make the theme consensus. Until then, the theme is under-owned relative to how much of the spending it captures.

underowned.title: Small and mid-cap biotech
parts: Attention Gap

Large-cap pharma and obesity drugs absorb most of the health-care attention. Citigroup says small and mid-cap biotechs are an alternative to large caps as it starts coverage [[n9445]], which is a sell-side view that has not yet reached the retail conversation.
Exposure & Risk

The biotech ETF is down 4.45% over 20 sessions at 85.97 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), less than the S&P 500’s 8.76% fall over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the group is holding up better than the market. The instrument risk is liquidity and the clinical-event binary, which is why position sizing matters more than the thesis.
Trigger to Watch

Approval decisions on the named small-cap drugs, such as the rare-disease product that is nearing a decision [[n9695]], would bring the theme into the consensus. Until then the group is a stock-picker’s market.

underowned.title: Copper as a grid and AI capex metal
parts: Attention Gap

Gold gets the record-high coverage [[n9506]], while copper is treated as a tariff trade. Citigroup’s call that LME copper reaches $10,000 before tariffs bite [[n9446]] is a sell-side view that treats copper as more than a tariff trade.
Exposure & Risk

Copper closed at 4.90 USD a pound, up 4.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the copper miners ETF is down 1.64% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The risk is that the miners lag the metal, so the cleaner exposure is the metal itself, not the equities.
Trigger to Watch
A tariff decision on refined copper, or a grid-capex announcement tied to data-centre power, would move the theme from under-owned to consensus. Copper is an asset here, not a read on China’s growth.

underowned.title: Japanese wage-led domestic demand
parts: Attention Gap

The Japan debate is about the BOJ and the yield, while the wage round is quieter. Major firms agreed big pay increases [[n5398]], and the largest union group reports its biggest wage demand in over 30 years [[n5240]]. The domestic-demand beneficiaries get less coverage than the rate story.
Exposure & Risk

The Japan ETF is up 1.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), and the Nikkei 225 is down 5.58% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The risk is that the wage gains are cut back by the cost-of-living squeeze that services sentiment has already flagged [[n5310]].
Trigger to Watch
The May BOJ discussion, if it goes ahead [[n5238]], would make the wage story the consensus. A weaker outcome would show the wage gains are not translating into domestic demand.

crypto.title: Bitcoin’s bear market hits newcomers hardest
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 81,066.70 USD, down 15.67% over 20 sessions and 5.91% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-13). Ether is at 1,862.97 USD, down 29.95% over 20 sessions, and Solana at 123.29 USD, down 27.00% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-13). Dogecoin is down 31.02% over 20 sessions at 0.17 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-13). Reuters describes the drawdown as hitting newcomers hardest [[n1988]], and CoinDesk reports that bitcoin’s four-year compound growth rate fell to a record low of 8% [[n1886]]. The equity proxies are hit harder: Coinbase is down 35.43% over 20 sessions, Robinhood 35.58% and MicroStrategy 19.45%, while the spot ETF IBIT is down 17.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
New / Most Important

The institutional plumbing is still being built even as prices fall. Cantor Fitzgerald launched a $2 billion bitcoin financing business, with Anchorage and Copper as custodians [[n1780]], and Clearstream will offer bitcoin and ether custody [[n1799]]. Fidelity’s ether ETF has asked the SEC for permission to stake [[n1804]]. The political layer is noisier: the WSJ reports that the Trump family held deal talks with Binance after its guilty plea [[n2004]], and Fortune reports that half a dozen cabinet members hold bitcoin assets [[n2010]]. Ripple and the SEC are reportedly near resolution of a four-year lawsuit [[n2042]].
Playbook

Prefer spot exposure to the equity proxies while the drawdown runs. The support levels analysts flag are $74,000 [[n1869]] and $70,000 [[n1915]], and the leveraged crypto equities, COIN and HOOD, tend to break first if those levels go. Strategy’s preferred stock has bucked the downturn in the common [[n2045]], which makes it the cleaner balance-sheet expression if the crowd wants one. The call changes if bitcoin closes back above its 20-session reference of 96,125.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-02-21).

flows.title: Liquidity is tightening at the front end and leaking into credit
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is being set by policy rates moving in different directions. The ECB cut to 2.5% [[n3354]] and markets price a further cut [[n3317]], the BOJ is leaning toward hikes [[n5305]], and the Fed is in no hurry [[n11433]]. China’s bond yields rose as cuts were priced out [[n1188]]. The US liquidity read comes from household balance sheets: household wealth reached a record high in the fourth quarter on stock gains [[n11920]]. That cushion makes a funding shock less likely to become a credit event, although the equity drawdown this month has taken some of it away. Balance-sheet news is not the marginal driver here; the policy rate is.
Rates & Dollar

The bond market is paying for the growth scare. TLT is up 3.92%, IEF up 2.79% and SHY up 0.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a bull steepening that reflects duration demand. The dollar index is at 103.83 index points, down 3.81% over 20 sessions, while EUR/USD closed at 1.0886, up 4.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Bessent called the dollar’s fall a natural adjustment [[n4051]], and a weaker dollar is being described as part of Trump’s plan [[n11932]]. USD/JPY closed at 148.2790, down 3.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the yen has strengthened against the dollar.
Credit Check

Credit is where the stress shows. US corporate bond spreads hit their widest in about six months on recession fears [[n3950]], and Goldman Sachs says spreads will get a lot wider amid tariffs [[n3916]]. Bloomberg reports that a massive unwind has made US junk bonds a riskier bet than Europe’s [[n3841]]. HYG is down 1.00% over 20 sessions while LQD is up 1.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so investment grade is holding and high yield is not. The consumer-credit read is consistent: fintech lenders are being sold on worries about consumer spending and credit [[n6290]]. The debt-supply question sits behind the credit read, and Ray Dalio warns that mounting US debt problems could lead to ‘shocking developments’ [[n3857]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Flows show dip-buying in mega-cap tech and de-risking among hedge funds. Investors bought a Magnificent Seven ETF amid the downturn, according to the data Reuters cites [[n6506]]. Hedge funds sped up de-risking, and Reuters says there is likely more to come [[n3918]], while Asia hedge funds outperformed their US peers as markets sold off [[n3978]]. Goldman Sachs says hedge funds have given up half of their 2025 gains in challenging markets [[n3628]]. Buybacks are the corporate bid: Dave announced a $50 million repurchase [[n3714]] and Metropolitan Bank $50 million [[n3933]], and Allegro proposed a $364 million buyback [[n5576]]. Italian asset managers’ net inflows doubled year on year to 6 billion euros in February [[n3838]], a sign that European savers are not yet selling. New issuance is paused as well: venture investors who hoped for an IPO recovery in 2025 now see it on hold [[n3952]].
Portfolio Implication

Hold duration, keep investment-grade credit, and reduce high-yield and leveraged fintech exposure while spreads widen. Back buybacks only where cash flow supports them: Allegro’s buyback comes with a guidance raise, which makes it more credible than buybacks announced into weak outlooks. Keep a small Asia long, since the Asia hedge-fund group outperformed on the sell-off [[n3978]], and cut the EM bond beta if the dollar rebounds. Size fintech and venture-linked exposure small until the new-issue window reopens, since issuance is usually the first thing to close when spreads widen. The implication flips if the stopgap passes and spreads retrace.

anticipatory.title: The US funding deadline and the shutdown trade
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a deal, though not with certainty. Schumer will clear the way for the spending bill [[n11891]], while House Democrats reacted with a ‘deep sense of outrage and betrayal’ [[n11934]]. The deadline is Friday [[n11929]], and the index is already in correction [[n11858]].
Conditional Expression

If the stopgap clears on time, the relief goes to duration first. TLT is up 3.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), so the trade is to own the bull steepening with a small equity add into oversold cyclicals. If it fails, the trade is cash and short-dated Treasuries, with the Nasdaq 100 the first to give back gains.
Risk

A shutdown is typically short-lived for markets, but the risk is that it compounds a tariff shock. Watch for a move in the 10Y that reverses the 35 bps rally over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13).

anticipatory.title: Tariff escalation against the June summit track
parts: What Is Priced

Retaliation is now concrete: the EU’s counter-tariffs on $28 billion of US goods [[n11761]], Canada’s C$29.8 billion of retaliation [[n4720]], and the threatened 200% wine tariff [[n11914]]. Against that, Washington and Beijing are discussing a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1359]].
Conditional Expression

If the summit track holds, the trade is long China consumption and Hong Kong equities, where the Hang Seng is up 7.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). If retaliation spreads, the trade is the defensives, with the Consumer Staples ETF down only 1.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13) and the yuan as the funding offset.
Risk

The risk is a whipsaw driven by announcements. Trump is targeting China-made containerships [[n1404]], and the US has struck back at China’s maritime trade with a port fee [[n1300]], so the escalation has more than one front.

anticipatory.title: Ukraine ceasefire talks in Moscow
parts: What Is Priced

Putin has set conditions on a ceasefire and wants direct talks at the White House before any ceasefire [[n4929]], while a US team is in Moscow for talks [[n4979]]. The market is pricing optionality, not a settlement.
Conditional Expression

If the talks move, the trade is European defence and Polish defence names with the budget story intact, and European autos are the cost-side loser in the rotation. If the talks stall, the trade is Rheinmetall’s momentum, up 70.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), with a tactical trim into the news.
Risk

Reversal risk is high. The Kremlin says the US-proposed ceasefire would ‘give nothing’ to Russia [[n4974]], and Putin has voiced doubts and set conditions on the same proposal [[n4928]]. A ceasefire read as a counter-proposal can turn the defence trade quickly.

anticipatory.title: A Bank of Japan hike in May
parts: What Is Priced

The 10-year JGB yield is at its highest since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5305]], and Reuters reports that a rate-hike discussion could come in May [[n5238]]. The market is pricing a hike path that the economy has not yet confirmed, and the yen is the transmission channel: USD/JPY is down 3.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Conditional Expression

If the BOJ moves in May, the trade is yen longs and the banks, with exporters as the hedge. If the May discussion fades, the trade is to buy Japanese duration and exporters, where Toyota is down 2.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
Risk

Wage data are strong, with major firms agreeing large raises [[n5398]], but growth is soft, with Q4 GDP downgraded [[n5308]]. The risk is an early hike into a growth downturn that tariffs are already deepening.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — GTC showcase into a sector drawdown
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The dated catalyst is the 2025 Nvidia GTC conference, where suppliers are lining up announcements [[n9560]]. Nvidia held up better than the Magnificent Seven peers during Thursday’s rout [[n6603]], which is the relative-strength signal behind the thesis. The thesis is that the stock leads the chain back once the GTC news flow starts.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Nvidia closed at 115.58 USD, up 4.53% over five sessions but down 11.87% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The hurdle is the 131.14 USD reference from 12 February. The risk is the valuation argument that Yahoo Finance reports a commentator makes, that Nvidia lacks the earnings and cash-flow capacity to justify its market cap [[n3098]].
Trade Expression

Buy the shares into the GTC window. The thesis is invalidated if the semiconductor ETF, at 195.10 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), breaks lower, since Nvidia’s relative strength has to hold against the basket.

catalysts.title: $ALE.WA — buyback and 2025 guidance
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Allegro expects rising 2025 earnings and proposed a $364 million buyback on 13 March [[n5576]], and the Polish press reports double-digit profit growth [[n6115]]. The thesis is that the buyback and the guidance reset the stock after its 20-session climb.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Allegro closed at 32.38 PLN, up 13.61% in the prior session and 5.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The hurdle is the 30.82 PLN reference from 13 February, and a fade back there would undo the buyback signal. The risk is that the one-session jump is a gap, and the guidance is already in the price.
Trade Expression
Buy on a pullback toward 30.82 PLN, with the thesis invalidated below that level, since a close there would mean the buyback has failed to hold the stock.

catalysts.title: $ADBE — guidance reset and AI monetisation doubts
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Adobe’s first-quarter beat came with a dull forecast that raised AI monetisation doubts [[n3006]], and CNBC put the drop at 14% on concerns about AI growth [[n3109]]. The thesis is that a guide that under-promises on AI revenue invites a multiple cut, and that post-earnings drift works against the stock.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Adobe closed at 377.84 USD, down 13.85% in the prior session and 18.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The reference is 462.76 USD from 12 February, which the stock would need to regain to reverse the thesis. The risk is that the sell-off already prices the guide, and a software-sector rebound could support the shares.
Trade Expression
Short the stock or buy puts into any strength, with the thesis invalidated if Adobe reclaims its 462.76 USD reference.

catalysts.title: $INTC — new CEO and the foundry question
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Intel named Lip-Bu Tan as CEO [[n9541]], and the stock jumped nearly 15% as investors cheered the turnaround [[n9539]]. A report that TSMC pitched a foundry joint venture to Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom [[n8806]] adds a structural question the new chief executive has to answer, which is why the thesis is mixed.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Intel closed at 23.70 USD, up 14.60% in the prior session and 5.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The reference is 22.48 USD from 12 February. The risk is that a one-day gain of this size is a turnaround premium that can reverse on execution doubts, and the WSJ’s profile of the chief executive’s approach is the bull case [[n9797]].
Trade Expression
Hold a small position and add only on a pullback to the 22.48 USD reference. Trim into any move that extends the one-day spike, since the thesis depends on execution rather than the appointment.

catalysts.title: $SOFI — the Blue Owl loan platform
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

SoFi agreed a loan-platform deal of up to $5 billion with Blue Owl Capital Funds [[n6620]], which moves personal loans off the balance sheet and gives the fintech a funding partner. The thesis is that the capital-light model earns fees while the credit risk sits with the partner.
Price Hurdle & Risk

SoFi closed at 11.39 USD, down 4.45% in the prior session and 22.88% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The reference is 14.77 USD from 12 February. The risk is that fintech lenders are being sold on consumer-credit fears [[n6290]], and the sell-off can outrun the deal.
Trade Expression
Buy in two tranches, and invalidate the thesis if the fintech lenders’ sell-off deepens and the partner terms come under review, since the deal is only as good as the funding it secures.

catalysts.title: $COST — biggest drop in three years, wage costs
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Costco’s stock had its biggest one-day drop in more than three years [[n3022]], and its hourly wage now reaches $31, with raises over the next two years [[n2898]]. The thesis is that wage costs are a margin question, but membership remains the moat, which is why the call is mixed.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Costco closed at 890.62 USD, down 3.93% in the prior session, 13.25% over five sessions and 16.38% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The reference is 1,065.12 USD from 12 February. The risk is that discount trade-down is shifting spending toward cheaper formats [[n4002]], which can hit the warehouse premium.
Trade Expression
Buy a starter position on weakness, with the thesis invalidated on a breakdown in the staples group. The 1,065.12 USD reference is the bull case’s hurdle, not a near-term target.

retail_intro: The dominant popular trade is Tesla, the stock retail refuses to sell after a 28.48% fall over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), a loyalty trade that resembles the Tesla rally of 2019–2020, the GameStop squeeze of 2021 and the Nvidia rebound of 2023 in the way a loved name’s own holders become its price floor.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — retail can't quit its love
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story retail tells itself is simple: Tesla is the company that made the mass-market electric car, and its stock has been cut in half, so the fall reads as a sale on a franchise rather than a verdict on it. CNBC reports that retail investors cannot quit their love for the stock [[n6606]], and Business Insider reports that with the stock cut in half, its investors want their chief executive back [[n6368]]. The hook is loyalty to the founder, whose name is the brand, and the crowd treats each bounce as proof the franchise survives the politics. The anchor is the 336.51 USD close of 12 February, the level the stock has to recover to end the drawdown (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13).
What Is Driving It

Tesla closed at 240.68 USD, down 2.99% in the prior session, 8.64% over five sessions and 28.48% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The move is an earnings and demand story as much as a politics story. JPMorgan cut its price target on Tesla, expecting lower deliveries [[n8976]], and Business Insider reports that JPMorgan analysts call the decline one for the history books [[n9175]]. China is the sharpest signal: Tesla’s China shipments tumbled [[n1278]], and the New York Times reports that China is cooling on Musk, with the ‘two cars for the price of one’ complaint [[n9435]]. Tesla also warned it could face retaliatory tariffs [[n9727]]. Cross-asset, the tape is risk-off: the S&P 500 is down 8.76% over 20 sessions, the Nasdaq 100 down 11.48%, and the VIX sits at 24.66 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), while the 10Y has fallen 35 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-13). That is the backdrop against which the stock’s 28.48% decline sits.
The Social Signal

Attention looks like loyalty under pressure. Retail investors are not leaving, per CNBC [[n6606]], and Quartz reports that even Tesla’s biggest bull says patience with Musk is ‘wearing very thin’ [[n6497]]. Fortune reports that the mega-bull Dan Ives warned Musk that patience is wearing thin [[n6416]]. The crowd reads that as the bulls still being on the team. A CNBC survey shows 85% of investors think Musk’s politics are having a negative or extremely negative effect on the company [[n6537]], so the loyalty sits beside a broad view that the brand is damaged. Ron Baron says he will not sell a single personal share despite the decline [[n8364]]. On the other side, Business Insider’s owners say embarrassment and fear are why they are selling their cars [[n9477]], and ABC reports Tesla vehicles vandalised across the US [[n9726]], the protest side of the same attention. Dip-buyers tend to tune out the protest noise and read the price, which is the crowd’s logic in one line.
Historical Analog

The closest mechanical analogue is the 2019–2020 Tesla run, when many professional investors called the stock overvalued while a loyal retail base kept buying the pullbacks, and the second wave of buyers arrived once the trend had visibly turned. The sequence is what matters. The first group that holds through the fall sets the floor. The second group, newcomers who see a stock that has already turned, supplies the next leg. Nvidia’s 2023 run follows the same order: a company whose story was real had its loyal holders absorb the drawdown before the wider crowd came back. What is different now is the political channel, which gives the drawdown a brand-level cause that a pure valuation argument does not resolve.
Smart Money View

Institutions are split on direction, and that split is more useful than the bull or bear label. The bull camp includes Ron Baron, who keeps his own shares [[n8364]], and Dan Ives, who still calls the company a mega-bull while warning on patience [[n6416]]. The skeptic camp includes JPMorgan, which cut its target and expects lower deliveries [[n8976]], the WSJ, which says the stock still is not cheap [[n11905]], and pension managers who worry as the shares fall [[n7964]]. New York state senators have urged the state pension fund to begin divesting from Tesla [[n8286]], which is the institutional pressure to watch. For some the disagreement is about direction, whether the business is impaired. For others it is about pace, whether the decline is too fast to reverse soon, and the WSJ’s line that the stock still is not cheap is the pace argument.
When the Narrative Breaks

The narrative breaks on observable levels and dated events. First, the price level: a close back above the 336.51 USD reference from 12 February would show the crowd has won the argument (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Second, a close below 240.68 USD while the S&P 500 is still falling would confirm the brand damage is still compounding. Third, the event list: the retaliatory tariffs Tesla warned about [[n9727]] and the deliveries JPMorgan expects to come in lower [[n8976]] are the data that could break the loyalty trade. Fourth, the instrument risk. Retail-heavy momentum names fall fastest when the index breaks, and the leveraged Nasdaq fund TQQQ is down 32.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13), which shows how fast leverage unwinds.

retail.title: D-Wave / QBTS — the quantum breakthrough
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The breakthrough story is the simplest one in the market right now. Investopedia reports that quantum stocks soared as D-Wave claimed a breakthrough [[n6518]], and Stocktwits flagged the surge under the line that retail braces for an exponential rally [[n6560]]. Reuters reports that D-Wave’s upbeat forecast sent quantum shares higher [[n3158]], and Business Insider says the stocks rebounded from a dip after a new ‘supremacy’ announcement [[n9088]]. The crowd’s story is that one breakthrough re-rates the whole category, so every quantum name is a proxy for it.
Where It Breaks

The move is single-name, not a basket move. D-Wave closed at 6.91 USD, up 18.73% in the prior session, 32.12% over five sessions and 14.40% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). Rigetti is down 25.53% and IonQ 43.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The break is a close back under the 6.04 USD reference from 12 February. Sceptics are active in the sector: PCMag reports scientists question Microsoft’s quantum ‘breakthrough’ [[n7630]], and Scientific American argues that scientists, publishers and investors create the hype [[n9520]]. The instrument risk is equity supply: IonQ halted its at-the-market programme after a $372 million raise [[n6470]], which is the company selling into strength.

retail.title: Oklo / OKLO — nuclear for the data-centre boom
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The power story is the newest version of the AI trade. Amazon, Google and Meta support tripling nuclear power by 2050 [[n6479]], and World Nuclear News frames the same goal across Amazon, Google, Meta and Dow [[n8697]]. Stocktwits reports that NuScale and Oklo surged on the big-tech bet, but retail sentiment pulled back [[n6515]]. The crowd’s simple story is that hyperscalers need firm power, and the small-reactor names are the cheapest way to own it. Alphabet’s chief investment officer says Google aims to cut the cost of new nuclear with small reactor deployments [[n6268]].
Where It Breaks

Oklo closed at 23.95 USD, down 8.55% in the prior session and 55.96% over 20 sessions, against 54.38 USD on 12 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). NuScale is down 42.39% over 20 sessions at 15.21 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-13). The break is a close back above the 54.38 USD reference, or a failure of the group to hold while the big-tech announcements keep coming. The sceptical marker is Utility Dive’s note that US small-reactor deals remain elusive for NuScale [[n2524]], and Reuters’ CERAweek piece says small nuclear power is struggling at the cusp of the electricity demand boom [[n6573]]. The instrument risk is a low-priced, high-volatility name in a sector where one contract can move the stock.

retail.title: Dogecoin / DOGE — internet jokes as an asset class
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Memecoins are the crypto trade with the most cultural pull. TradingView calls memecoins crypto’s cultural engine, built from internet jokes [[n6511]]. Robinhood is listing new tokens such as PENGU and POPCAT as crypto activity ramps up [[n6609]], and Yahoo reports a new meme coin, Cocoro, launched by Dogecoin’s IP rights holder [[n1723]]. The crowd’s story is that the joke is the asset, and the platform that lists the next one wins the attention. Decrypt reports that President Trump’s own Solana meme coin is down 85% from its peak [[n1728]], which the crowd reads as the memecoin cycle turning rather than ending.
Where It Breaks

Dogecoin closed at 0.17 USD, down 4.24% in the prior session, 14.11% over five sessions and 31.02% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-13), against 0.24 on 21 February. The break is a close back above that reference, or a slide below the 0.16 support analysts flagged [[n1696]]. The regulatory trigger is live: Coinbase will suspend memecoin trading for Floki, Turbo and Gigachad in New York [[n1994]], and a WilmerHale note on meme-coin regulation sets the compliance backdrop [[n2049]]. The instrument risk is liquidity, which can vanish quickly, and a delisting from a major venue removes the exit for retail holders.
